title: Hawaii volleyball outlasts Wyoming in 5-set thriller | University of Wyoming | wyomingnews.com
text:
LARAMIE — Three weeks ago, Kaylee Prigge stomped off the court, infuriated from a sweep loss against Mountain West preseason favorites Texas El-Paso.
A five-set battle against league-leading Hawaii three weeks later presented an opposite feeling.
Hawaii outlasted the University of Wyoming 25-13, 19-25, 26-28, 25-18, 17-15 on Thursday night at the UniWyo Sports Complex.
Yet, Cowgirls coach Prigge viewed the comeback bid as an encapsulation of what her team could be.
“I told our group, that is actually most proud of I have been of them the entire season,” Prigge said. “We just went toe-to-toe with the No. 1 team in the league. Against a formidable opponent, we took advantage of an opportunity that we didn’t take against UTEP in weekend one in conference play.
“I thought we finally lived into what should be always our identity, which is defense.”
The Rainbow Wahine (15-3 overall, 7-0 Mountain West) ran its win streak to seven and snapped the Cowgirls’ (10-8, 3-4) three-match win streak.
Paige Lauterwasser paced the Cowgirls with 13 kills on a night where they hit .075 compared to Hawaii’s .176.
“Offensively, we have got to be a little bit better,” Prigge said. “More well-rounded. We were very one-dimensional and that is just how it was because we couldn’t get enough people going.”
Hawaii posted 21 blocks to UW’s 13.
Addy Thorington and Ruby Jensen helped the Cowgirls with 11 kills apiece.
“We talk a lot about how we just want to reflect on past successes,” Jensen said. “I feel like tonight was a really big success for us. We talked about how proud we are of each other and our coach is proud of us.”
UW battled an onslaught of Hawaii attackers as Cha’lei Reid (16), Panna Ratkai (14), Maeli Cormier (12) and Miliana Sylvester (11) boasted double-digit kills.
Hawaii pulled through a fifth set that included 11 ties.
"It is a lot more deflating when you get your ass kicked by UTEP, who was voted No. 1 in the league,” Prigge said. “You are right effing there against (Hawaii), who is right now No. 1 in the league. We show up again on Saturday. That is a choice and we got to live into who we are.
“I think that was our coming out party. I think that is the turning point in our season right there.”
A lopsided first-set loss fueled the Cowgirls’ comeback attempt.
Multiple scoring sources in the second set and closed it on a 5-2 run, then endured a marathon third set that featured multiple ties — including at 22, 23, 24, 25 and 26.
The Cowgirls ended that frame on a 3-0 run.
Hawaii punctuated the fourth set, thanks to Sylvester’s kill. The Rainbow Wahine dug out of a 3-0 hole in that frame, then tied things at five before they never relinquished their lead.
Hawaii’s front line posted seven blocks in the first set.
That advantage helped Hawaii close the first frame on a 15-3 run. The Cowgirls hit –0.071 in a first set that included nine attack errors.
The Cowgirls host Hawaii at 6:30 p.m. Saturday.
